title: Museum of Quietness
venue: THEMUSEUM, Kitchener, Ontario — presented within "SONICA – A Sound Experience"
description:
[NOTE: Luisa's latest CV lists a 2021 THEMUSEUM project with Kanika Gupta under the title "Sound Print," linking to THEMUSEUM's "SONICA – A Sound Experience" exhibition page. This is very likely the same work as "Museum of Quietness" from the old Squarespace site, but confirm which title is current before publishing.]

A participatory art experience inviting audiences to examine the auditory and visual noise in their surroundings, then design their own artifacts imagining a quieter future and their role in creating it. Presented in person at THEMUSEUM and virtually over Zoom for pandemic-isolated participants.

title: One Day They Will Return
description:
[NOTE: this project does not appear in Luisa's latest CV paste — confirm it should still be included before publishing.]

A speculative fiction project imagining a world where birds mysteriously vanish, prompting humanity to build elaborate nests decorated with bird memorabilia in hopes of their return — exploring environmental collapse, collective denial, and humanity's attempts to restore what has been lost through sculptural installations, sonic environments, and immersive storytelling.

title: Wishing Well
description: A participatory soundscape and live sonification work. Materials: borrowed objects from local shops, reclaimed roof tiles from the Hsinchu City Railway Warehouse, contact mics, and a bio-sonification module. Sound design by Luisa Ji and Benjamin Lappalainen; production support from Husna Farooqui.

title: Sediments
venue: Residency: DAÏMÔN / Radio-Hull; Performance: Place-des-artistes de Farrellton
description: Environmental sonification and collected soundscapes derived from local ecosystems near Wakefield, Quebec. Performed with Hooria Rahimi at River Room, a spatial installation by Rahimi.

title: When Spiders Spin Dusk
venue: Research and Creation: June–September 2024, residency at Ferme Lanthorn, Wakefield, Quebec; Exhibitions: Toronto 2024 (The Bridge), Seoul 2025 (Coréana Museum of Art, Space*c)
description:
[NOTE: the Seoul venue (Coréana Museum of Art, Space*c) is carried over from an earlier scrape of Luisa's residencies list, not from her latest CV paste directly — confirm it's the correct Seoul exhibition venue before publishing.]

A program design project — a residency at Ferme Lanthorn that resulted in a duo-city exhibition. Six artists based in Canada and Korea jointly researched and developed works on themes concerning geological shifts, cultural perspectives on AI, and technology's relationship to the more-than-human world. International co-production with Junghyun Kim, with funding from the Canada Council for the Arts and Arts Council Korea. See the two companion Writing pieces (spiralling-outwards, carnival-of-shipwreck) rather than duplicating that text here.

title: Shipwreck
description: A durational presentation format centring on the question of "how do we make a home among ruins?"
